fields.description:
Measured while proving the MCP OOM root cause on witted-invisible-roan (9ea3-7d07-ea55-4496). Not a memory defect — a latency one — but it lands on the same ~60s MCP client deadline whose ambiguous timeout causes duplicate billed gate runs (bug d80d-7be7-1c0a-4231), so it is filed rather than left as an aside.

## Observed

Against a local `rebar-mcp` (Streamable-HTTP, readonly) over a full clone of this store (8,879 ticket dirs):

| condition | `show_ticket` latency |
|---|---|
| server idle | **41.7s**, then 39.9s warm |
| while 8 concurrent `ready_tickets` are in flight | **80.5s** |

For comparison, a whole-store `ready_tickets` compile on the same server is 16.3s. A single-ticket read is therefore ~2.5x more expensive than compiling the entire store.

## Mechanism

`resolve_ticket_id` falls through to `_scan_alias` whenever no prebuilt `alias_index=` is supplied (`src/rebar/_ids.py:458-460`). `_scan_alias` (`src/rebar/_ids.py:312`) does `os.listdir(tracker)` and then calls `_effective_alias_for_dir` for EVERY ticket directory, each of which does its own `listdir` plus a `json.load` of that ticket's CREATE/SNAPSHOT event.

So resolving one id costs a full-store directory walk and ~8,900 JSON parses. The only caller that supplies a prebuilt index is `commit_impact.py:211/233`, so essentially every MCP tool call that names a ticket pays this — and project policy is to WRITE aliases, which is exactly the input that takes the scan path.

## Why it matters beyond latency

1. The MCP client deadline is ~60s. A 40s idle floor means an ordinary `show_ticket` is already inside the same order of magnitude as the timeout, and 80s under a concurrent read burst is over it. A `-32001` timeout is the ambiguous non-signal that provokes duplicate, double-billed gate re-runs (`AGENTS.md`, "Long gate ops over MCP").
2. It is the dominant allocator churn on the read path (tens of MB of parsed dicts per resolution), feeding the same RSS high-water mechanism proven on 9ea3.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: `show_ticket` on an idle server against a store of this size completes in a small fraction of its current 40s, measured before and after with the same harness.
- [x] AC2: id resolution no longer parses every ticket's CREATE/SNAPSHOT to resolve one id — verified by counting `json.load` calls (or file opens) during a single resolution, before and after.
- [x] AC3: resolution semantics are unchanged across every accepted id form — alias, full canonical id, two-quad short id, legacy single-quad, and Jira key — including the ambiguity and not-found paths, proven by a differential test over the real store comparing old and new resolution for a large sample of ids.
- [x] AC4: a held-out regression test fails before the fix and returns to failing when the fix is perturbed.

## Notes

The natural direction is an alias index built once per store revision rather than per call, but the resolver has ordering/shadowing rules (`_effective_alias_for_dir` exists because an alias can be re-pointed), so AC3's differential check over the real store is the load-bearing part, not the index itself.

## Completion evidence

The fix is already merged on main as 1798b4429135be7597669622e0fbaf82d441757b (`Resolve one alias without a whole-store scan`, Gerrit Change-Id Ifc81914bae526a73ba10a81c1d8622d7ef3d4e40). It added a process-local resolver scan cache and regression coverage in `tests/unit/test_single_id_alias_resolve_scan_cache.py`. Targeted validation in `../fix4-durational` on 2026-09-06: `pytest tests/unit/test_single_id_alias_resolve_scan_cache.py -q` => 7 passed.
